evidence.claim: Model knowledge: existing control-room displays can be configured to group status and equipment references without automating operator commands.

assumptions: Boundary is operator preparation, exact instruction and live signalling/acknowledgement. Other workers' physical pump or valve work remains outside the focal denominator and earns no saving.

Control systems already produce tagged timestamped status; procedure owners supply current procedures and a contact roster. s1 retains verification and manual lookup when references are missing; no new sensor or worker-location feed is assumed.

OTHER is the existing control-room process display. Native read-only configuration first; no model loop or write to controls. The gate is the operator's own positive-time authorisation of an already formed instruction, not a new manager approval.

Any change in instruction, target, worker or relevant conditions requires renewed verification before transmission. Live dialogue remains fully retained; no automatic message, log write or additional report is proposed.

tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated asset references and general-purpose report fields can add work around physical maintenance and escalation.
tasks.enabler_now: Native forms can reuse existing asset metadata without inventing a malfunction or inferring completed repairs.
tasks.still_hard: Diagnosing a physical fault and knowing when work exceeds the operator's scope remain human responsibilities.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise an unresolved equipment problem and describe the actual condition accurately.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: maintenance forms can reuse asset and routing metadata while operators capture actual work and fault observations.

assumptions: This provisional episode includes permitted operator maintenance followed by reporting an unresolved malfunction. Report-only or successful-maintenance-only cases need different measured shares; do not force both branches into every occurrence.
Boundary includes actual maintenance, report preparation and supervisor delivery. Repair scheduling and specialist repair are other-role work outside the focal denominator and yield no saving.

Asset owners already supply equipment id and location; supervisors maintain routing recipients. s3 retains fourteen hours for all actual condition, work-performed and access-constraint capture. Missing identifiers are entered manually there; no free inspection data is assumed.
Native configuration first. The proposed reduction touches only form navigation and repeated metadata. No physical work, supervisor conversation or diagnostic judgement loses time.

Shares and reductions are unmeasured scenarios, not historical baselines. Same-system save and short send remain fully retained. The report is complete before approval; any later edit requires renewed approval.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: process views can display current movement identifiers and existing tagged meter readings together; physical routing and instrument health still require verification.

assumptions: Boundary includes reference lookup, physical and instrument checks, assessment and its existing movement verification record. No route change, meter calibration or repair is proposed.

Movement owners supply id, product, direction and intended meter; operations owns versioned mappings, and the installed control system supplies tag, value, unit, time and quality. s1 checks missing mappings manually, s2 produces actual field observations and s5 counts their capture.
OTHER is the existing process display. Native configuration first; missing tagged readings remain unavailable rather than generated. No machine action relies on an uncaptured field observation.
Shares and reductions are provisional scenarios, not measured baselines. Saving concerns navigation and numeric/identifier comparison, not existing sensor runtime, physical inspection or judgement.

The existing verification record is a scenario assumption, not a newly invented saving baseline. Its actual capture and same-system save remain fully retained. Any needed separate problem report must be counted once with the monitoring/reporting task in roll-up.
